summary.oneLiner: A clean, predictable "growth + profitability + predictability" quarter: total AUM +25% YoY to Rs 1,06,940 cr (Growth AUM +32%, now 98% of book), consol PAT +67% to Rs 461 cr, and Growth-business RoAUM up to 1.9% (from 1.5%) driven almost entirely by a 57 bps opex-ratio improvement. Cost-to-income fell to 53% (from 66% a year ago). Asset quality is remarkably stable (retail 90+ at 0.7%, in a 0.6-0.8% band for 4+ years). Two new signals: an AA→AA+ domestic upgrade (unlocks larger-ticket mortgages + higher leverage) and an *early, hedged* flag on IT-sector salaried stress in South India. Board approved an enabling Rs 4,000 cr capital raise.

one-line thesis: A clean, predictable "growth + profitability + predictability" quarter: total AUM +25% YoY to Rs 1,06,940 cr (Growth AUM +32%, now 98% of book), consol PAT +67% to Rs 461 cr, and Growth-business RoAUM up to 1.9% (from 1.5%) driven almost entirely by a 57 bps opex-ratio improvement. Cost-to-income fell to 53% (from 66% a year ago). Asset quality is remarkably stable (retail 90+ at 0.7%, in a 0.6-0.8% band for 4+ years). Two new signals: an AA→AA+ domestic upgrade (unlocks larger-ticket mortgages + higher leverage) and an early, hedged flag on IT-sector salaried stress in South India. Board approved an enabling Rs 4,000 cr capital raise.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > NIM QoQ optics: ~10 bps is a 90- vs 91-day EMI-calendar artifact; a further ~17-20 bps is a deliberate choice to do less direct-assignment (DA) sell-down ("DA is a pinch-hitter"). Underlying yield stable at 13.2-13.4%. Retail did NOT show the usual Q1 seasonal deterioration.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: FY27 guidance reaffirmed (AUM growth, profit growth, RoAUM) — "confident of meeting original guidance provided last quarter"; Growth AUM sustaining in the 30s%.
RoAUM: 1.8-1.9% (Q1) → 2.5% by exit Q4 FY27; lever = larger year-end book on flat people cost (staff increments front-loaded in Q1).
Opex/AUM: retail at 3.5%, to move further lower through FY27; ~40-50 bps more value over next 4-5 quarters.
Gold loans: 67 branches (Q1) → 200 branches by end-March 2027 (phase-2 launched).
PL branch penetration: to ~100% "over next 2-3 quarters."
Leverage: 4.5-5x long-range goal (set when AA-rated; likely revised higher as AA+ beds in).
Capital: board-approved enabling raise up to Rs 4,000 cr, "at an appropriate time post shareholder approval" (growth capital; CAR comfort floor ~18% vs 15% regulatory).
order book & pipeline — n/a (financial): Disbursements +44% YoY. Retail franchise 6 mn customers (+24%); cross-sell = 28% of unsecured disbursement (target materially higher). Branches 780 (net +79): gold 67, rural 178, urban 535 (closed 8 full-service urban). Wholesale disbursed Rs 2,604 cr across 73 transactions (38 new); repayments Rs 1,932 cr (74% of disbursed) — ~61% of FY27 contractual wholesale repayments already prepaid.
segment / subsidiary detail: Mortgages Rs 61,199 cr (+30%) = 57% of company / 67% of retail AUM; mass-affluent HL + larger-ticket "LAP Plus" growing fastest (AA+ upgrade enables serving these). Small-ticket affordable housing demand organically weak (industry low-single-digit/negative).

Unsecured Rs 21,412 cr (+45%) across PL, UBL, digital/embedded, rural micro — 20% of company AUM. Risk at best levels in 2+ years; rural micro at all-time-best ratios. Digital (embedded/FLDG, 80%+) is high-beta on volume; Fintech activity picked up last 2 quarters.

Wholesale Rs 13,238 cr (+27%), RE:CMML 70:30, yield 14.2% (moderating on better rating mix). Elevated prepayments = real-estate cash flows running ahead of underwriting + CMML bank refinance/capital-market takeouts — a growth headwind but a quality signal.
Legacy Rs 2,452 cr (2% of AUM), down Rs 355 cr.
growth verticals / optionality: Gold loans (67→200 branches by Mar-27) + rural micro (branch build-out); cross-sell scale-up (lower opex/credit cost); larger-ticket secured mortgages post-AA+; embedded/digital finance (capital-light, FLDG). Possible inorganic M&A ("Piramal house has used M&A for value creation"; open but nothing imminent, unrelated to the raise).
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona: Affordable-housing cost leadership: operating at ~12.5% in <Rs 35 lakh housing — management frames Piramal itself as "the disruptor over the last 4-5 years" in that segment, not a victim of competition. AA+ rating structurally lowers cost of funds vs affordable-HFC peers.

Enterprise AI at genuine scale: 320 bn AI tokens in Q1 (vs 178 bn Q4, 63 bn a year ago) at flat token cost (mix-shift to homegrown SLMs/open-source); credit-staff productivity +50% in 2 years. Launched "Pia," an AI investor-relations assistant (claimed first-of-kind external tool). Credible operating-efficiency moat (cost-to-income 72%→53% in 2 years).
margins & cost dynamics: NIM 6.5% (Growth 6.8%); the QoQ softness is DA-choice + calendar, not pricing. Cost of borrowing 8.80% (-4 bps QoQ) with AA+ tailwind ahead; minimal CP exposure cushioned dislocated Q1 wholesale funding markets. Opex +10% vs revenue +37% — the operating-leverage engine (opex/AUM down 3.5 yrs straight). Floating-rate mortgages: no PLR cut through the down-cycle, so lower rate-cut pass-through obligation on the way up ("lower amplitude both ways").
capex / expansion — n/a (financial): Investment = branch network (gold/rural) + AI stack. Gold 22→67→200 (Mar-27) branches; consolidating urban full-service branches even as it adds specialist branches.
capital allocation: CAR 18.85% (all Tier-1); enabling Rs 4,000 cr raise for growth (management comfort floor ~18%; consumes ~63 bps/qtr). Chose not to do Tier-2 (shallow market, poor rates). Large "hidden" regulatory capital (~Rs 9,000 cr delta: DTAs + Shriram/Pramerica investment book) to be released over time. M&A optional, not imminent.
risks & watch-items: IT-sector salaried stress, South India — early-bucket bounces up (13% of unsecured salaried base); counter-intuitively visible in secured, not unsecured; "breaking news," no flow to deeper buckets yet — underwriting already tightened on the margin.
LAP — small Q1 uptick (4 idiosyncratic cases); "seat belts on," Q2 started well.
Small-ticket housing demand organically weak industry-wide.
Wholesale prepayments structurally cap wholesale AUM growth.
West Asia conflict: no visible portfolio impact yet (possible lag).
management quality / tone: Framework-disciplined (Growth/Profitability/Predictability), high-disclosure, self-critical. Jairam repeatedly hedged the IT-stress signal ("take it as breaking news … don't make too much of it") — flagged proactively rather than buried. Honest on NIM optics (DA pinch-hitter, calendar effect) and on PCR being an ECL output, not a target. Youngest upper-layer NBFC framing (retail phase ~5 yrs post-DHFL) used to argue a long profitability-expansion runway.
non-obvious takeaways: The RoAUM story is an opex story, not a yield story — 57 bps of the 33 bps RoAUM gain came from opex ratio; yields are flat by design.
IT-salaried stress showing in secured before unsecured is the genuinely novel, non-consensus data point — inverts the usual stress-transmission and is worth tracking sector-wide.
Wholesale "headwind" (61% of FY27 repayments already prepaid) is actually a portfolio-quality flex — RE cash flows beating underwriting.
Capital raise is pre-emptive (enabling), not need-driven — 18.85% CAR is comfortable; the ~Rs 9,000 cr locked regulatory capital (DTA + Shriram book) is a future ROE unlock.

Next Q → check: RoAUM path to 2.5% exit-Q4; IT-salaried stress — flow into deeper buckets / spread beyond South?; LAP 90+ (does the Q1 uptick persist?); capital raise executed?; gold-branch build toward 200; PL branch penetration to ~100%; AA+ cost-of-borrowing benefit showing up; wholesale AUM vs prepayment drag.
